title: Why worry, mind
hookLine: kaahe re man chitveh udam: why plot and scheme, mind, when even creatures in the rocks are fed (Gujri M5, ang 10)

lines: WHAT IF, WHAT IF, WHAT IF.
A SHABAD FOR THE WORRIED MIND.
cards: Two in the morning. The house is dark and everyone else is asleep, but your mind is wide awake and running scenarios. What if the job falls through.
What if the test results are bad. What if I say the wrong thing tomorrow. You plan, re-plan, rehearse arguments that haven't happened.
None of it changes anything at two a.m. Guru Arjan knew that mind. And he wrote it a shabad that starts with a question.

teach.h: KAAHE RE MAN: WHY SCHEME, MIND?
teach.b: It opens: kaahe re man chitveh udam. Why, mind, do you plot and scheme, when the dear Lord Himself has taken care of your keeping? Then the picture that gives us today's line.

teach.h: IN THE ROCKS, FOOD PLACED BEFORE THEM.
teach.b: In rocks and stones, the shabad says in paraphrase, He created living beings, and He places their food in front of them.
Think of a tiny creature living in a crack in a rock, nowhere near a field or a market, and still it's fed.
Then the refrain: whoever meets the true congregation is carried across, and by the Guru's grace, even dry wood turns green. Then a harder line.
Mother, father, friends, children, spouse: no one, finally, is anyone's support. The Lord provides for each and every head, so why are you afraid, mind? And another picture.

teach.h: A BIRD FLIES FAR; WHO FEEDS THE YOUNG?
teach.b: A bird flies hundreds of kos, the old measure of distance, leaving its young behind. Some translators make it a crane. Who feeds them?
Who teaches them to peck? They remember her, the shabad says. It closes: all treasures and powers lie in the palm of the Lord's hand; Nanak is forever a sacrifice; You have no limit.
Does this mean don't work, don't plan? No. Sikh life is built on kirat karni, honest work, and elsewhere gurbani praises effort.
The word here is about the anxious scheming of a mind that thinks everything depends on it alone. Do your work.

teach.h: WORK HONESTLY; PUT THE WORRY DOWN.
teach.b: Then put the two a.m. worry down.

how: Kaahe re man chitveh udam is the fifth shabad of Rehras Sahib, recited each evening; Sikhs pair its trust in the Lord's provision with kirat karni, earning an honest living.

o: a question to the mind: why scheme and fret?
a lament that the Lord has forgotten us
a warning to stop working and planning

p: who feeds them, who teaches them?
turns green by the Guru's grace

s: this shabad tells Sikhs not to work or plan
Sikh life is built on honest work; the shabad addresses anxious scheming.
the shabad says even creatures inside rocks are given their food
their sustenance is placed in front of them.
the shabad is by Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru
it's in Raag Gujri, the fifth shabad of Rehras.

games.q: it's 2 a.m. and your mind is scheming about tomorrow. what question does Guru Arjan put to it?
o: have you planned for every outcome?
why scheme, when even creatures in the rocks are fed?
why not stay up and work it out?
games.why: kaahe re man chitveh udam: why plot and scheme, mind, when the Lord Himself provides for all.

practice: Name one worry that's been riding with you, hold it in your mind like a stone in your hand, and feel how heavy it is.

Ask whether there's one honest thing you can do about it, then picture setting the stone down beside you: it's still there, you're just not carrying it right now. If you pray, you can say Waheguru once, and let the hand stay open.

wordCard.voice: Why worry. Kaahe re man chitveh udam: Guru Arjan asks the anxious mind why it schemes, when even creatures in the rocks are given their food.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: rijak, sustenance, daily bread; the Lord places it before even the creatures in the rocks.

carryVoice: Your line: even the rock-creatures eat. Honest work, yes; the anxious scheming, no. Rest easy tonight.

sources.ref: Gujri M5, kaahe re man chitveh udam, Ang 10
